h1:
Edible Souvenirs from Sa Kaeo
Melon, Wang Nam Yen Milk, Mu Yo & Processed Treats + Where to Buy
intro: Sa Kaeo is a more fun place to shop for edible souvenirs than most people expect. There's melon and cantaloupe from the farms around Aranyaprathet that come out fragrant, sweet and crisp; fresh milk from the big Wang Nam Yen dairy cooperative; OTOP-award mu yo sausage from Wattana Nakhon; Ban Phrao sticky rice grilled in bamboo; and processed snacks like santol candy. We've gathered what locals in Sa Kaeo actually buy, with the neighborhoods, shops, and ballpark prices so you can pack the good stuff home without missing it.

blocks.html: When people think of Sa Kaeo, they tend to picture Rong Kluea Market and shopping along the border. But ask what there is to eat and bring home, and the answer is a lot longer than that. This province is one of the country's biggest melon and cantaloupe growing areas, home to the Wang Nam Yen dairy cooperative that produces some of Thailand's top milk, and it still has local processed foods made by families who've kept the recipes going for years. So we've rounded up the full list of edible souvenirs from Sa Kaeo, along with where to find each one.

The souvenirs below are ordered from the items that are signature to the province and easy to find, down to the local-only ones you'll need to track down at the source. The prices given are rough ranges that shift with the season and size. For fresh items like melon and grilled sticky rice, ask about the production date and shelf life before you buy them for a long trip home.

blocks.text: Edible Sa Kaeo Souvenirs Worth Bringing Home

items.name: Aranyaprathet Melon & Cantaloupe
items.blurb: The edible souvenir that's basically the face of Sa Kaeo. Aranyaprathet is the largest cantaloupe-growing area in the country, and the variety people talk about most is Sun Lady — fragrant, with crisp sweet flesh that keeps longer than other types. You'll also find green- and orange-fleshed melons from the greenhouse farms. Pick a fruit whose base is still slightly firm so it ripens just right by the time you get home.
items.meta: Aranyaprathet · grown year-round in greenhouses · fresh, eat within 3–5 days
items.price: ฿80–180 per kg depending on variety and grade

items.name: Wang Nam Yen Fresh Milk & Dairy Products
items.blurb: The Wang Nam Yen dairy cooperative is one of Thailand's biggest milk producers, and the "Wang Nam Yen" brand is easy to find — pasteurized fresh milk, UHT milk, and processed products like yogurt and milk tablets. It's a souvenir locals here are proud of: easy to buy, easy to carry, and a hit with kids. A low-key gift that still wins people over.
items.meta: Wang Nam Yen / Wang Sombun district · sold at the co-op storefront and in souvenir shops
items.price: Milk bottle/carton ฿15–35 · milk tablets/processed items vary by pack

items.name: Wattana Nakhon Mu Yo (Vietnamese Pork Sausage)
items.blurb: The signature souvenir of Wattana Nakhon district, made from pure pork — firm and springy with a balanced flavor. The maker with a 5-star OTOP award is Mu Yo Wattana, offering the original recipe, a black-pepper version, and mu yo with pork skin. Another well-known name is Pho Mu Yo Wattana Nakhon, which has a storefront. Buy it by the log; it keeps in the fridge for several days.
items.meta: Wattana Nakhon district · 5-star OTOP · keep refrigerated, chill it on the way
items.price: ฿50–120 per log depending on size and recipe

items.name: Ban Phrao Sticky Rice in Bamboo (Wattana Nakhon)
items.blurb: Famous grilled sticky rice in bamboo from Ban Phrao, Wattana Nakhon district. The maker people mention is Pa Bang's stall, with white sticky rice, black sticky rice, and a custard-topped version — sweet and rich, soaked in coconut milk and roasted in fragrant bamboo tubes. Grab some warm along the way. Best eaten day-of, not for carrying several days.
items.meta: Ban Phrao, Wattana Nakhon · fresh, eat same day
items.price: ฿20–40 per tube depending on size and filling

items.name: Santol Candy (Wan Dee Souvenir Shop)
items.blurb: An unusual processed-fruit snack that Wan Dee Souvenir Shop highlights as its specialty — a chewy santol candy they say only they make, with a chewy texture that's sweet with a tart edge and fun to snack on. It keeps far longer than fresh fruit, making it a one-of-a-kind edible gift. The shop has a storefront in town and ships online via its Facebook page and Shopee.
items.meta: Sa Kaeo town · storefront + online orders · keeps well

items.name: Vietnamese Mu Yo, Naem & Fermented Treats (Aranyaprathet)
items.blurb: Aranyaprathet has a large Thai-Vietnamese community, so there's mu yo, naem (fermented pork), and Vietnamese-style fermented foods to bring home. The shops locals mention are Yai Tem, Je Aot, and Je Rang, around Mit Samphan Road in downtown Aranyaprathet, selling mu yo, spring-roll wraps, and fermented items as sets. A souvenir with a distinct Vietnamese flavor.
items.meta: Mit Samphan Road, Aranyaprathet · fermented/processed, keep refrigerated

items.name: Ta Phraya Melon (Grown on Lalu Soil)
items.blurb: In Ta Phraya, growers plant melon on the lalu eroded-soil terrain that's unique to this side of the province. The flesh is sweet and crisp, and pre-orders pile up in some seasons. It's an edible souvenir tied to Ta Phraya's unusual landscape. If you're heading to the Lalu site or Ta Phraya National Park and hit harvest season, drop by and support a local farm.
items.meta: Ta Phraya district · seasonal, check the harvest cycle with the farm first

items.name: Melon Products (Juice, Smoothies, Jam)
items.blurb: Many melon farms, both around Aranyaprathet and along the Wang Nam Khiao border, have a cafe zone that turns melon into juice, smoothies, ice cream, and in some cases jam or dried melon to sell as souvenirs. Great for people who want the melon flavor without carrying whole fruit — sit and eat at the farm, then take the processed version home.
items.meta: Aranyaprathet melon farms / Wang Nam Khiao border · cafes on-site at the farms
items.price: Drinks ฿40–80 per glass · processed items vary by pack

items.name: Seasonal Fruit (Santol, Jackfruit, Mango)
items.blurb: Besides melon, Sa Kaeo has seasonal orchard fruit that villagers bring out to sell along the road — santol (the raw material for the santol candy), jackfruit, and mango. During harvest there are roadside stalls at several points along the main routes, cheaper than buying in town. Worth grabbing if you pass through when the fruit is in.
items.meta: Roadside stalls on main routes · seasonal
items.price: ฿20–80 per kg depending on type and season

items.name: Sweets & Souvenirs from Big-Name Shops in Town
items.blurb: Downtown Sa Kaeo has souvenir shops that combine processed foods and sweets in one place — like Wan Dee Souvenir Shop and others stocking mu yo, santol candy, processed fruit, and local sweets. Ideal if you're short on time and want to buy everything in one shop before heading home. We'd ask about the production date on fresh items before picking them up.
items.meta: Sa Kaeo town · everything in one shop
items.price: Varies by type, from ฿30 per bag and up

blocks.title: How to pick a good melon or cantaloupe
blocks.html: Smell the base of the fruit — if it's fragrant, it's close to perfectly ripe. If you're carrying it for several days, choose one whose base is still a little firm and let it ripen on the way. Cantaloupe with a clear, even netted skin is usually sweeter. For green-fleshed melon, press gently at the stem end — if it gives just slightly, it's just right.

blocks.text: Main Places to Buy, by Neighborhood

items.name: Aranyaprathet
items.blurb: The hub for melon, cantaloupe, and Vietnamese fermented foods. There are melon farms around Ban Fak Huai and fermented-food shops along Mit Samphan Road. A good stop before or after hitting Rong Kluea Market and the border checkpoint.

items.name: Wattana Nakhon
items.blurb: Home of Wattana Nakhon mu yo and Ban Phrao sticky rice. There are mu yo storefronts and roadside sticky-rice stalls — easy to stop at while driving through on the main route.

items.name: Wang Nam Yen / Wang Sombun
items.blurb: Source of Wang Nam Yen milk from the dairy cooperative. Buy fresh milk and dairy products at the co-op storefront. Handy if you're passing through the southern part of the province.

items.name: Sa Kaeo Town
items.blurb: Souvenir shops that gather many things in one place — santol candy, mu yo, processed fruit, and local sweets. Good for buying everything in one shop before you head home.

blocks.text: Melon Farms You Can Buy from On-Site

blocks.html: If you want fresh melon straight from the farm with a walk through the greenhouses, the Aranyaprathet side has farms that welcome visitors — like Malee Melon Farm at Ban Fak Huai, Aranyaprathet, which grows melon and seedless watermelon in greenhouses without chemicals and offers tastings and several varieties to buy. Along the border with Wang Nam Khiao (Korat), there are also several melon farms with cafes out front where you can sip melon juice before taking fresh fruit home. We'd check the farm's Facebook page for the harvest cycle and opening days before going, since fresh fruit comes out in rounds.

items: Malee Melon Farm — Ban Fak Huai, Aranyaprathet; grown in greenhouses, with several varieties to taste and buy
Melon farms on the Wang Nam Khiao border — cafes out front serving melon juice and smoothies, plus fresh fruit and processed products to buy
Ta Phraya melon orchards — grown on lalu soil, a local highlight; a good stop if you're visiting Lalu and Ta Phraya

blocks.title: Fresh items to carry home need to stay cool
blocks.html: Melon, sticky rice, mu yo, and fermented foods can spoil if left in a hot car for long. If you're driving back a long way, bring a cooler bag or ice packs. Fermented items and mu yo should be eaten within a few days and kept chilled the whole time. Sticky rice in bamboo is best the same day — don't keep it for several days.

blocks.text: If You're Stopping by Rong Kluea Market / the Border

blocks.html: Many of Aranyaprathet's edible souvenirs are near Rong Kluea Market and the Khlong Luek checkpoint — both the melon farms and the Vietnamese fermented-food shops — so a lot of people roll it all into one trip. But if you plan to cross the border or shop the market on the border side, check the current border situation and get your travel documents in order before you actually go, since the rules and checkpoint opening hours can change. Buying edible souvenirs on the Thai side, meanwhile, works as usual without crossing the border.

faq.q: What's the most famous edible souvenir from Sa Kaeo?
faq.a: Melon and cantaloupe from Aranyaprathet are what people think of first, since this is the largest cantaloupe-growing area in the country, and the fragrant, sweet, crisp Sun Lady variety is the favorite. After that come Wang Nam Yen milk from the dairy cooperative, Wattana Nakhon mu yo, and Ban Phrao sticky rice in bamboo.

faq.q: Where can I buy Sa Kaeo melon, and how much does it cost?
faq.a: You can buy it at melon farms around Aranyaprathet, such as Malee Melon Farm at Ban Fak Huai, farms on the Wang Nam Khiao border, and orchards in Ta Phraya. Prices run about ฿80–180 per kg depending on variety and grade. The fruit comes out in rounds, so check the farm's Facebook page for the harvest cycle before going.

faq.q: Where do I buy Wattana Nakhon mu yo, and does it keep long?
faq.a: You can buy it at storefronts in Wattana Nakhon district. The maker with a 5-star OTOP award is Mu Yo Wattana, with several recipes — original, black pepper, and mu yo with pork skin. It keeps in the fridge for several days; if you're carrying it a long way, keep it chilled in transit to preserve the flavor and freshness.

faq.q: Are there souvenirs that keep well for a long trip?
faq.a: Yes. Santol candy from Wan Dee Souvenir Shop is a processed fruit that keeps a long time and travels easily. Mu yo and Wang Nam Yen milk tablets also keep reasonably well. Fresh items like melon, sticky rice in bamboo, and fermented foods should be kept cool and eaten within a few days.

faq.q: Where should I go to get everything in one place?
faq.a: Downtown Sa Kaeo has souvenir shops that gather many things together, such as Wan Dee Souvenir Shop with santol candy, mu yo, processed fruit, and local sweets. Good for people short on time who want to finish their shopping in one stop. We'd ask about the production date on fresh items before picking them up.
